question: If an original cloud breakout was too large for its observed first-window turnover, can the same account recover the missing exposure at the next 12H decision?
source: Frozen OKX v1.7 12H VIX-ranked nine-parent account, 1000 USDT, 10% of median turnover across the last 60 closed one-minute bars, same 1585 positive original parents. A separate causal shadow account supplies the initial cap-binding and the net 12H profitability gate under the same costs; the traded account must also have really hit its own first-window cap.
single_variable: At the first subsequent finished 12H close, attempt one market purchase of remaining collateral shares in still-open children in proportion to their current units. Use immediately following native open after higher priority normal open exits. At this hour a scheduled per-parent trim preempts the addition. Limit by the unfilled initial planned nominal amount, observed next window capacity, spare 20% of opening portfolio equity remaining after current parent nominal, and free cash divided among one top-up and every currently empty original parent slot. Never restore size lost to an interim trim or partial exit. Source-unknown gets no new fill.
arms: Leave original as reference. Restrict top-ups to net profitable originally cap-bound open shadow parents. Test the complementary net nonpositive group as a direction control. Fee only and 5bp on all market executions. New fills are taker 5bp. Original stops and preassigned exits remain. Confirm all frozen funded and hourly ledgers when additions disabled.
scope: Historical OKX funding and exit/orderbook depth unavailable. Fixed reference portfolio used elsewhere in research. Final account surplus / 1000 must strictly exceed 1000, wins at least 20%, drawdown upper bound at most 50%.
